# `hs-run test` — state map

<!-- generated by render_state_map.py — edit the SSOT, # learn: "${HARNESS_BIN_ROOT:-.}"/harness/data/hs-run-registry.d/<domain>.yaml, not this file -->

Every state `hs-run test` can report, with what it means. Run the CLI, read the `state`, do the judgment that state names, run it again — each state is re-derived from artifacts on disk, so deleting an artifact regresses the state.

This file is generated. Change the source named in the comment above, then re-render with `render_state_map.py`; edits made here are lost on the next render.

## States that route something

The CLI hands these rule and reference paths over at the moment the step begins — the body does not repeat them.

| state | what it means | routes |
|---|---|---|
| `no_stack_detected` | No language marker anywhere under the root. Which command counts as "the tests" is a judgment nothing on disk settles — ask the user rather than guessing one. | `claim-verification` |
| `stack_no_test_cmd` | The stack is recognised but declares no runner. Different from finding nothing: there IS a project here, and the missing piece is one declaration in its own manifest — ask for the command, or for where it belongs. | `claim-verification` |
| `deps_missing` | A required dependency is not importable. The install command is in the envelope; nothing about the suite is knowable until it runs. | `claim-verification` |
| `deps_stale` | Everything imports, but a required package sits outside its declared range — the tier a plain import check cannot see, where the break arrives at the first real call rather than at load. Pin the ranges before reading any result. | `claim-verification`, `verification-mechanism` |
| `ready` | A stack is detected, it declares a test command, and every required dependency is installed inside its declared range. The command is in the envelope; run it, then read the result against the rules this state carries. | `regression-sentinel`, `sampled-rate-reporting`, `mutation-proof`, `tdd-discipline`, `references/coverage-and-edge-cases.md`, `references/qa-report-format.md` |
| `no_plan` | No plan directory, so a verification has nowhere to live — and the hard stage gate blocks on its absence even when the suite is fully green. Open a plan before treating a green run as shippable. | `claim-verification` |
| `no_verification` | A plan is open and no verdict is written yet. This is the step that writes one: the QA report shape and the artifact contract are what the envelope carries, because getting either wrong is caught two stages later by the push gate. | `verification-mechanism`, `plannotator-review-gates`, `references/qa-report-format.md`, `references/verification-artifact.md` |
| `verification_malformed` | A verdict is written and the push gate would reject it as written — a non-canonical check name, or a result file it cannot re-derive from. The problems are listed in the envelope; fix those exact lines. | `verification-mechanism`, `references/verification-artifact.md` |
| `verdict_unbacked` | A PASS is recorded that re-derivation does not support: a check names a result file that is missing or failing, or the change class requires a test type no check covers. The exact reason rides in the envelope — close that, then record what the suite actually did. The push gate reads the same evaluation, so this is the same block arriving one stage earlier. | `claim-verification`, `tdd-discipline`, `references/verification-artifact.md` |
| `verified` | PASS recorded, checks re-derived from a real result file. Hand off. If the plan carries a coverage grid, fold its verdict in as one advisory line — it never flips a test verdict. | `claim-verification`, `references/grid-consume.md`, `references/delegation-route.md` |
| `suite_failed` | A FAIL is recorded. Fix the code, or fix a test that is genuinely wrong and say why — the one thing that is never on the table is deleting or weakening a test to reach green. Whether this red was written on purpose is not on disk; you know which it is. | `tdd-discipline`, `regression-sentinel`, `references/regression-and-build.md`, `references/delegation-route.md` |
